cons_torah.label: Torah · Common melody
cons_torah.sub: The common Eastern-European (Lithuanian) Torah melody, from a Conservative congregation’s printed chart
cons_torah.note: The “common melody” of most Conservative and Orthodox synagogues in America (the Lithuanian–Polish Torah tune, as codified by Rosowsky and taught at JTS). Transcribed from a Conservative congregation’s printed learner’s chart; its page 5 (pazer, yetiv, zakef gadol and the first zarka–segol rows) was not available, so those rows are missing.
cons_torah.source: A Conservative congregation’s printed learner’s chart of the common (Lithuanian) Torah melody, pages 1–4 and 6 (page 5 was not available)
cons_torah.license: The melody is traditional. This transcription is CC BY-SA 4.0.

cons_haftarah.label: Haftarah · Common melody
cons_haftarah.sub: The common Eastern-European haftarah melody, from a Conservative congregation’s printed chart
cons_haftarah.note: The haftarah tune of most Conservative and Orthodox synagogues, written here with one flat (the mode centres on D, with the characteristic lowered seventh). Transcribed from a Conservative congregation’s six-page learner’s chart; rhythms are the chart’s own.
cons_haftarah.source: A Conservative congregation’s six-page printed learner’s chart of the common haftarah melody
cons_haftarah.license: The melody is traditional. This transcription is CC BY-SA 4.0.

spiro_hhd.label: High Holy Day Torah · Spiro
spiro_hhd.note: Pinchas Spiro’s High Holy Day Torah trope chart, widely used in Conservative congregations. Notes in parentheses are the chart’s optional pickups for unstressed syllables; the chart writes no key signature and spells the mode with B♭ and F♯ as needed.
spiro_hhd.source: Hazzan Pinchas Spiro, High Holy Day Torah trope chart (20 lines)
spiro_hhd.license: The melody is traditional. This transcription is CC BY-SA 4.0.

je_torah_western.label: Torah · Western Ashkenazi
je_torah_western.note: The Torah tune of the German and English (“Western”) Ashkenazi synagogues as sung in London around 1900; this is the line Trope Trainer calls British – Western Europe. Transcribed from the cantillation tables of the Jewish Encyclopedia (1901–06, art. “Cantillation”, Francis L. Cohen), which set each tradition’s rendering of every sign side by side. The table gives each sign in a standard context, so these rows are the table’s columns regrouped into phrases.
je_torah_western.source: The Jewish Encyclopedia (New York: Funk & Wagnalls, 1901–1906), article “Cantillation” (Francis L. Cohen), the cantillation tables: “Ashkenazim, 1902”
je_torah_western.license: The table is in the public domain (published 1901–1906). This transcription is CC BY-SA 4.0.
